# CV-15 — Channel lifecycle and permissions

> Branch `t/maciej/cv-15-lifecycle-2` · status: built, migration applied locally, ready to land
> Migration: `supabase/migrations/20261016140000_chat_v2_channel_lifecycle.sql` · applied to the local stack 2026-10-16 after CV-12's `20261016120000_chat_v2_chains` and CV-10's `20261016130000_chat_v2_references`. The seven functions it redefines were checked against their live bodies first (CV-12 and CV-10 change none of them). `bun run db:test chat` passes (18 files, incl. chat_chains and chat_links).

## Delivered against the row

- **Server** (one migration): `chat_op_set_manager` (managers and admins add and remove managers; the person must be in the channel in a role that posts; the last manager in effect can't be removed, themselves included), `chat_op_set_announcement` (channels only; `share_op_announce` keeps v1's refusals and goes through it until CV-23), `chat_op_make_private` (one way; General stays public; people who read it without being in it lose it and their open Catch up items close as `closed`), `chat_op_delete_channel` / `chat_op_restore_channel` / `chat_recently_deleted` (30 days; General and direct messages refuse; a name taken meanwhile (create and rename's rule) comes back as "… (restored)"), `chat__purge_deleted` (channels only, never direct messages) + the hourly `chat-purge-deleted` job (25 at a time). Redefined from their live bodies: `chat_op_remove_member` (the removal is recorded whether the person was in it, had left, or only read the public channel; their open items close; the quiet `removed` line), `chat_op_add_members` (the quiet `added` line), `chat_op_join` / `chat_op_leave` (the roster stamp), `chat_op_archive_channel` (archiving closes the channel's open items).
- **New columns:** `chat_channels.roster_at` (people or managers changed: readers re-read People and managers on it, never on a message), `chat_channels.purged_at`, `chat_members.access_at` (the conversation's readers changed: the member's own row tells their copy to check access), `chat_catchup.channel_name` (an added / removed line names the channel even after you can no longer read it).
- **Client:** Details "As a manager" (frame 4): Manager labels in People, + to add people (private: managers; public: anyone who posts and is in it), each person's ⋯ (Make manager / Remove as manager / Remove from channel), the Channel settings block (Only managers can post, Private one way with the one confirm, Name and topic → Edit, Archive channel, Delete channel with a confirm). Recently deleted from the left panel's ⋯ (Restore, days left). Reply privately in an announcement channel's message menu. The role editor's chat rows (Settings → Members → Roles). History lines for every new op. Store and runtime ops for each; `chat_recently_deleted` in `READ_RPCS`.

## Agent's choices (deferred to by Maciej: confirmed for building, may be reconsidered)

- **A removal from a public channel sticks** (they can't join or post again until a manager or admin adds them back), and is recorded whether they were in it, had already left it, or had only read it · agent · one rule for public and private, and a removal that a click on Join undoes would mean nothing · rejected: a public removal that only ends the current membership.
- **The purge erases content but keeps tombstones**: messages, Catch up items, managers, notices, history and links go; the channel row stays with no name or topic and its membership rows stay, stamped as left · agent · membership rows are only ever stamped, never deleted, so each person hears only about their own row · rejected: a hard delete of the channel row (its memberships would go with it).
- **The announcement switch's history op is `chat.announcement_switch`** with `{ on }` · agent · `chat.announcement` is already an announcement's bell row (CV-5) and History hides it · rejected: reusing it.
- **Reply privately puts the post's link in the direct message's draft** rather than sending it at once · agent · the spec's "opens a direct message to the author with the post quoted": the reply is theirs to write, and a sent link with nothing after it would ping the author for nothing · rejected: the brief's open-then-send.
- **The announcement line's "Reply privately" answers the newest post in view** (a top-level message by someone else): a direct message to its author with the post in the draft, like the message menu's; with no such post in view, a direct message to one of its managers · agent · CH50 "a direct message to the author with the post quoted" · rejected: CV-8a's group message with every manager.
- **Recently deleted shows in the left panel's ⋯ for anyone who posts**; the list holds only what they may restore (often nothing for a member) · agent · knowing whether someone manages any channel would need another read on every open · rejected: a per-open managers read.
- **A person's manager actions live on a ⋯ on their row in Details' People** (Make manager / Remove as manager / Stop managing / Remove from channel), shown to managers and admins · agent · frame 4 draws the Manager labels but no control for them; the row is where the person already is · rejected: the person card (its actions are the person's, not the channel's).
- **Archive moved into Channel settings** (frame 4's danger zone, beside Delete); an archived channel shows no settings, so Unarchive stays in the footer · agent · frame 4 · rejected: keeping CV-8b's footer button.
- **+ in People for a public channel shows to anyone who posts and is in it** (§12: members add people to public channels); a private channel's to its managers and admins.
- **Recently deleted for admins lists only channels they could have read** (public, or private ones they're in) · agent · Manage any channel never reveals a private channel · rejected: every deleted channel.
- **A restored public channel whose name was taken comes back as "<name> (restored)"** · agent · restoring never fails on a name · rejected: refusing until someone renames the other.
- **The announcement line follows the channel's managers, not "Manage any channel"**: an admin who isn't one of its managers sees "Only managers post here", as the server refuses their post (§12 footnote 1).
- **Creating a channel writes no "added" lines** for the people in it from the start · agent · the new channel arrives in their sidebar; the line is for being added to something that already exists · rejected: a line per creation.
- **The role editor's chat rows save one at a time** (as each switch flips), separately from the role's permissions draft, and only on the three built-in roles; a custom role shows Member's (Viewer's if read-only) without switches · agent · chat's switches are per built-in role (`workspace_chat_caps`), so they can't ride the role's own save · rejected: a draft shared with the permission matrix.
- **"Add custom emoji" is not shown yet**: `workspace_chat_caps` has no `add_emoji` column at the start of this block (CV-20 adds it). The brief says to hand back "blocked on CV-20" in that case; I built everything else instead, and the row appears by itself once the column exists (`visibleRights`). CHAT_CAPABILITIES and `CHAT_CAP_DEFAULTS` are untouched (CV-20's).

- **Only a role that posts can be made a manager, on the client too**: Details reads each person's workspace role and read-only flag (`mergePeople`, `personPosts`) · agent · chat's own read of people carries no role · rejected: hiding the item only for the built-in Viewer.
- **A manager row that manages nothing can be removed** even when no other manager is in effect · agent · removing it changes nobody's rights.
- **The purge runs hourly in batches of 25** · agent · one transaction per run, so small batches keep a large channel from holding back the rest · rejected: a daily run of 500.
- **Deleted channels are hidden from the connector.**

## Gotchas (area: supabase)

- A Realtime update on `chat_channels` reaches only those who can read the row afterwards: deleting or making a channel private reaches nobody that way. Stamp each member's own row (`access_at`) so their copy checks access.
- `module_activity` op `chat.announcement` is the bell's; don't reuse it for the switch.
- `entities_op_tombstone` checks links edit access: a chat manager may lack it; ops update `entities` directly.

## For later blocks

- **Known limits:** someone who only reads a public channel (no membership row) learns it was deleted or made private at their next access check, not live. Every join and leave moves `roster_at` (Details and managers re-read).

- **CV-11:** `added` / `removed` Catch up lines carry `actor_id` and `channel_name` (the removed person can't read a private channel's row); they're never counted. Archive and removal close items as `closed`.
- **CV-10:** Reply privately puts `moduo://chat_message/<id>` at the start of the direct message's draft: draw it as the card.
- **CV-16:** `chat_channels.roster_at` is the "who's in it changed" stamp; moving doesn't touch it.
- **CV-20:** add `add_emoji` to `workspace_chat_caps` and `chat_caps_set`; the role editor's row shows once the column exists.
- **CV-21:** Recently deleted and the lifecycle ops refuse keys (no session).
- **CV-23:** drop `share_op_announce`.
- **CV-9:** the purge doesn't touch attachments yet (chat files don't exist); add them to `chat__purge_deleted` with AT-1's trash clock.
- **Known limit (client):** a workspace role change (say member → viewer) reaches the chat screen only when the workspace's role is read again (a reload); the server refuses at once. Removing someone as manager is live (the roster stamp).
- **moduo-mcp:** the chat connector's channel reads skip deleted channels (`deleted_at`); deploy it with this migration.
- The account erasure's hand-over order still differs from `chat__hand_over` (CV-2-fix note); not changed here.

## Manual checklist (step → expect → surface)

- [ ] As a channel's manager open Details → Manager labels, + in People, Channel settings (two switches, Name and topic Edit, Archive, Delete) → web
- [ ] ⋯ on a person → Make manager → "Manager" appears; History "made someone a manager" → web
- [ ] As the only manager, ⋯ on yourself → Stop managing → refused: "A channel needs a manager…" → web
- [ ] Remove someone as manager while they have the channel open → their Channel settings disappear without a reload → web (two browsers)
- [ ] Turn on Only managers can post → a member sees "Only managers post here · Reply privately"; their message menu has Reply privately → it opens a DM to the author with the post's link in the box → web
- [ ] Turn on Private → the confirm "Make <name> private? It can't go back to public. N people stay in it." → the switch locks on → web
- [ ] Remove someone from a public channel → they can't Join it again from Browse → web
- [ ] Delete a channel → it leaves everyone's sidebar; ⋯ → Recently deleted lists it with days left → Restore brings it back → web
- [ ] Settings → Members → Roles → Member → Chat rows; flip Manage any channel → a member can archive any channel → web
- [ ] As a viewer → no Channel settings, no + in People, no Recently deleted → web

## Verify before release

- The purge job (`chat-purge-deleted`, hourly at :17) on staging with a channel deleted 31 days ago (set `deleted_at` back): content gone, the row and memberships kept as tombstones.
- Realtime on staging: a delete reaches members within a second through `access_at`.
- Prod grants for the redefined functions match the migration (authenticated + service_role, never anon).
